title: IELTS Listening Practice Test 1
description: Full IELTS Academic Listening test — 4 sections, 40 questions. Covers form completion, multiple choice, matching, and sentence completion.

parts.title: Section 1 — Leisure Centre Membership
parts.subtitle: A conversation between a new member and a leisure centre receptionist.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
A woman (Sarah) is calling the Greenwood Leisure Centre to enquire about and sign up for membership. She speaks with Tom, the receptionist.

Listen and answer Questions 1–10.

Questions 1–6: Complete the membership form below.
Questions 7–10: Choose the correct letter A, B or C.

questionGroups.title: Questions 1–6
questionGroups.instructions: Complete the membership form below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.explanation: The receptionist confirms the surname "Mitchell" and asks Sarah to spell it.
Sarah says her birthday is the fourteenth of March.
Sarah gives her house number as twenty-seven.
The receptionist repeats back "B14 6RQ" and Sarah confirms.
Sarah gives her mobile number as 07823 441 990.
Tom recommends the Gold membership and Sarah agrees to take it.

questionGroups.title: Questions 7–10
questionGroups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: What is included in the Gold membership that is NOT in the Silver membership?
questions.explanation: Tom explains that Gold members receive two free personal training sessions per month, which Silver members do not get.

questions.prompt: How much does the Gold membership cost per month?
questions.explanation: Tom says the Gold membership is fifty-five pounds a month.

questions.prompt: When can Sarah collect her membership card?
questions.explanation: Tom says her card will be ready to collect tomorrow, i.e. the following day.

questions.prompt: What does Sarah need to bring when she collects her card?
questions.explanation: Tom asks Sarah to bring proof of address, such as a utility bill.

parts.title: Section 2 — City Heritage Walking Tour
parts.subtitle: A tour guide describes a self-guided walking tour of a historic city district.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
A tour guide is presenting information about a free self-guided walking tour of Hartfield city centre to a group of visitors.

Listen and answer Questions 11–20.

Questions 11–15: Complete the notes below.
Questions 16–20: Label the map.

questionGroups.title: Questions 11–15
questionGroups.instructions: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
questionGroups.sharedContent:
HARTFIELD HERITAGE WALK — Visitor Notes

Duration of tour: approximately {{11}} hours
Route length: {{12}} km
Starting point: {{13}} Square
Best time to visit: {{14}} mornings (fewer crowds)
Audio guide app: download "{{15}}" before arriving

questions.explanation: The guide says the tour takes approximately two hours to complete at a leisurely pace.
The guide mentions the route covers three-and-a-half kilometres.
The guide instructs visitors to start at Cathedral Square.
The guide recommends visiting on weekday mornings to avoid weekend crowds.
The guide tells visitors to download the app called "Hartfield Heritage" on their smartphones.

questionGroups.title: Questions 16–20
questionGroups.instructions: What is located at each position on the map? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter A–H next to Questions 16–20.
questionGroups.sharedContent:
Map locations:
16. Position marked ★ near the river: ________
17. Building directly opposite Cathedral Square: ________
18. Large building at the north end of Market Street: ________
19. Small structure in the park: ________
20. Building at the corner of Bridge Lane: ________

A. Art Gallery
B. Old Courthouse
C. Roman Baths
D. Covered Market
E. Clock Tower
F. Silk Mill
G. War Memorial
H. Tourist Information Centre

questions.explanation: The guide says the Roman Baths are visible beside the river, marked on your map.
The guide identifies the Old Courthouse as the building directly facing Cathedral Square.

questions.prompt: Large building at the north end of Market Street
questions.explanation: The Covered Market is described as the large Victorian building at the northern end of Market Street.
The War Memorial stands in the centre of Riverside Park.

questions.prompt: Building at the corner of Bridge Lane
questions.explanation: The Silk Mill museum is located at the corner of Bridge Lane and the High Street.

parts.title: Section 3 — University Research Project
parts.subtitle: Two students discuss their group project on urban food waste reduction.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
Mia and Daniel are undergraduate students meeting with their tutor to discuss their research project on urban food waste reduction strategies.

Listen and answer Questions 21–30.

Questions 21–24: Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions 25–30: Match each strategy with its description.

questionGroups.title: Questions 21–24
questionGroups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: What aspect of food waste does Mia want to focus on?
questions.explanation: Mia says she is most interested in how supermarkets can donate or redistribute surplus food rather than discarding it.

questions.prompt: What does Daniel say is the biggest barrier to food waste reduction?
questions.explanation: Daniel argues that without stronger laws requiring businesses to report waste, voluntary initiatives will remain ineffective.

questions.prompt: What does the tutor suggest they add to their methodology?
questions.explanation: The tutor recommends including semi-structured interviews with managers at local supermarkets and restaurants to gather primary data.

questions.prompt: When is the final report due?
questions.explanation: The tutor confirms the submission deadline is in six weeks from the current date.

questionGroups.title: Questions 25–30
questionGroups.instructions: Which description (A–H) matches each food waste reduction strategy? Write the correct letter A–H next to Questions 25–30. There are more descriptions than strategies, so you will not use all of them.
questionGroups.sharedContent:
Strategies:
25. Community fridges
26. Dynamic pricing apps
27. Anaerobic digestion
28. Gleaning networks
29. Date label reform
30. Food banks

Descriptions:
A. Converts organic waste into biogas and fertiliser
B. Reduces confusion causing premature disposal of edible food
C. Allows consumers to buy nearly-expired products at a discount
D. Recruits volunteers to collect unpicked crops from fields
E. Provides shared refrigerated space for food donations in neighbourhoods
F. Connects surplus food with families in financial hardship
G. Requires businesses to publish annual waste audit reports
H. Encourages community gardens in urban areas

wordBank.text: Connects surplus with families in need

questions.explanation: Community fridges are described as shared refrigerated spaces placed in public areas where anyone can leave or take food donations.
Dynamic pricing apps allow stores to automatically reduce prices on items approaching their sell-by date to encourage purchase.
Anaerobic digestion is a biological process that converts food and organic waste into biogas (energy) and digestate (fertiliser).
Gleaning networks organise volunteers to harvest produce left in fields after commercial picking, preventing it from going to waste.
Date label reform aims to simplify and standardise "use by" and "best before" labels to reduce premature disposal of safe food.
Food banks collect surplus food from retailers and manufacturers and redistribute it to individuals and families in financial hardship.

parts.title: Section 4 — The Science of Sleep
parts.subtitle: A university lecture on sleep stages, functions, and the effects of deprivation.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
A professor delivers a lecture to first-year biology students on the science of sleep, covering REM and non-REM stages, the glymphatic system, and the cognitive effects of chronic sleep deprivation.

Listen and answer Questions 31–40.

Questions 31–40: Complete the lecture notes below.

questionGroups.title: Questions 31–40
questionGroups.instructions: Complete the lecture notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
questionGroups.sharedContent:
THE SCIENCE OF SLEEP — Lecture Notes

Sleep Architecture:
• Sleep cycles last approximately {{31}} minutes each
• Non-REM sleep has three stages; Stage 3 is called {{32}} sleep
• REM sleep is associated with {{33}} and memory consolidation

Functions of Sleep:
• The {{34}} system clears metabolic waste from the brain during deep sleep
• Growth hormone is released during {{35}} sleep (Stage 3)
• Immune function depends heavily on adequate {{36}}

Sleep Deprivation — Effects:
• After 24 hours without sleep, cognitive performance equals a blood alcohol level of {{37}}%
• Chronic deprivation is linked to increased risk of {{38}} disease
• Reaction time and {{39}} are among the first skills to deteriorate
• The body cannot fully {{40}} sleep debt by sleeping longer on weekends

questions.prompt: Sleep cycles last approximately ________ minutes each
questions.explanation: The professor states each complete sleep cycle lasts approximately ninety minutes.
Stage 3 non-REM sleep is referred to as slow-wave sleep due to the characteristic delta brainwave activity.

questions.prompt: REM sleep is associated with ________ and memory consolidation
questions.explanation: The professor explains that REM sleep is the stage during which dreaming predominantly occurs.
The glymphatic system, active primarily during deep sleep, flushes out toxic proteins such as beta-amyloid from the brain.

questions.prompt: Growth hormone is released during ________ sleep
questions.explanation: The professor notes that the majority of growth hormone secretion occurs during slow-wave (deep) sleep.

questions.prompt: Immune function depends heavily on adequate ________
questions.explanation: Studies show that people who sleep less than six hours per night are more susceptible to viral infections.

questions.prompt: After 24 hours without sleep, cognitive performance equals a blood alcohol level of ________%
questions.explanation: The professor cites research showing that 24-hour sleep deprivation impairs cognition to the same degree as a 0.10% blood alcohol concentration.

questions.prompt: Chronic deprivation is linked to increased risk of ________ disease
questions.explanation: Chronic sleep deprivation is strongly associated with elevated risk of cardiovascular disease, including hypertension and heart attacks.

questions.prompt: Reaction time and ________ are among the first skills to deteriorate
questions.explanation: The professor explains that reaction time and the ability to concentrate are among the first cognitive functions to be impaired by sleep loss.

questions.prompt: The body cannot fully ________ sleep debt by sleeping longer on weekends
questions.explanation: Research shows that while weekend recovery sleep offers some benefit, it cannot fully repay accumulated sleep debt or reverse all associated health effects.
